## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Apariyāpannakathā* (Kv 14.9) is the ninth discourse of the fourteenth chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The text addresses the controversial proposition: "May wrong views be found in the 'unincluded sphere' (*apariyāpanna*)?" [Nyanatiloka 2007]. This position is attributed to the Pubbaseliyas, who appear to interpret the designation *apariyāpanna* ("unincluded") loosely in the sense of "supra-sensual"—pertaining to the fine-material and immaterial spheres (*rūpa-* and *arūpa-dhātu*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. By contrast, the Theravādin debater adheres to the orthodox Abhidhamma definition, under which *apariyāpanna* designates strictly the supramundane consciousness (*lokuttara*) of the noble disciples (*ariya*), which is free from mundane defilements; the Theravādin counters that while an ordinary worldling (*puthujjana*) entering the *jhāna* states may be temporarily detached from sensual craving, they are not thereby exempt from wrong views [Nyanatiloka 2007].
